prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1350; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a rear-end collision at a signalled intersection and a knee injury. The claimant is not represented by an attorney, so all communication is directly with the claimant.

Entry 2: Police attended and filed a report. The responding officer and two independent witnesses stated that the claimant was not inside the vehicle at the time of impact, which conflicts with the initial account and needs follow-up.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both match the description of how the collision occurred. The other driver's insurer has been notified.

Entry 4: The claimant was asked to clarify their position at impact. In a follow-up call the claimant added a few minor details, such as the approximate speed and the lane positions, but the core account of events did not change.

Entry 5: The driver named on the policy confirmed the coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 6: No prior damage to the vehicle has been identified in the records or inspection. The repair estimate is under review, and it is not yet clear whether all listed damage came from this impact.

Entry 7: The claimant reported the knee injury after the collision and was seen at urgent care. The injury pattern appears consistent with the force and direction of the impact.

Entry 8: Medical records show a standard course of physiotherapy, and the claimant's reported pain has steadily decreased with treatment. No earlier injury to the same knee is known from the claimant's history or prior claims search.

Entry 9: Treatment is tapering off and the claimant reports improving mobility. The file will be reviewed again once the final treatment notes are received.

Entry 10: The claim remains open pending the repair estimate review and the resolution of the discrepancy about the claimant's position in the vehicle at impact.
